newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ayala, units unfazed by depreciation in peso.
newsitem.headline: Ayala, units unfazed by depreciation in peso.

text.p: Ayala Corp and its housing and telecommunications subsidiaries have not been affected by the recent peso depreciation, company officials said on Tuesday.
"Ayala Corp is fine, we have an exposure of $300 million -- that's very comfortable," Ayala president Jaime Augusto Zobel de Ayala told reporters after a special shareholders' meeting.
Ayala, a diversified holding group, provides monthly reserves for possible peso depreciation, he added.
The Philippine currency has fallen about eight percent since July 11 when it was effectively devalued.

Globe Telecom GMCR, Ayala's telecommunications joint venture with Singapore Telecom, said its aggressive capital expenditure programme would not be affected because this would be financed mostly through equity infusion.
The company has outstanding foreign loans worth $109 million.
"The depreciation really doesn't slow things down," Globe chief financial officer Gil Genio said.
Ayala Land Inc president Francisco Licuanan said the property business was affected by uncertainties in the foreign exchange market as well as the high interest rates.
However, he said Ayala would not be affected since it was not launching any projects at the moment.
"There is some hesitation when things like that take place ... People will step back and look at the situation. It's very visible in the secondary market," Licuanan said.
He believes interest rates will return to normal by the end of the year when the company hopes to launch a new project.
Licuanan added he was not concerned about the company's slower first-half growth. Ayala posted a five percent rise in net income, compared to 52 percent last year.
"It's a result of a very strong first half last year when there was a large transaction," he said.
Zobel de Ayala said the slowdown was expected after years of strong growth. "We're not concerned ... Any adjustment down should be expected."
Ayala shareholders approved the unification of its A and B common shares which will add liquidity in the market. The company has 5.66 billion outstanding A shares and 2.568 billion B shares.
